anomalies.observed: The 3.3 V LDO output is on net +3.3V, but no FCC2 or NAVC2 VDD/VDDA/VBAT pin is connected to either +3.3V or +3V3; those MCU power pins are in unconnected nets, and the +3V3 net itself has no regulator source.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that the 3V3 rail feeds both MCUs (FCC and NAVC) and the sensor ICs.

evidence.quote: 3V3 feeds both MCUs (FCC, NAVC) and all I2C sensor ICs

anomalies.impact: Both MCUs are unpowered, so the board cannot execute firmware, communicate, or control the aircraft.

anomalies.observed: The FCC HSE crystal is wired to FCC2 PE6/PE7 rather than PH0/PH1, and the NAVC HSE crystal is not connected to NAVC2 PH0/PH1; the MCU oscillator pins only have decoupling/reference-related nodes.
anomalies.expected: Both MCUs should use the 25 MHz HSE crystal on their OSC_IN/OSC_OUT pins (PH0/PH1 for these packages).

evidence.quote: HSE crystal (both MCUs) | FCC / NAVC | ABM8G-25.000MHZ-4Y-T3

anomalies.impact: The intended external 25 MHz clock is not connected; clock configuration may fail or fall back to HSI, causing timing/performance deviations.

anomalies.observed: The NAVC-side sensor I2C nets contain the IMU, magnetometer, barometer, temperature sensor, EEPROM, pull-ups and test points, but no NAVC2 pins; NAVC2 PB6/PB7 are unconnected. No signal net connects FCC2 to NAVC2.
anomalies.expected: The NAVC should be connected to its sensors and to the FCC via the shared UART/I2C/GPIO link described in the specification.

evidence.quote: NAVC↔FCC run UART2 + I2C + GPIO between the two MCUs

anomalies.impact: The navigation MCU cannot read its sensors or exchange data with the flight-control MCU, defeating the dual-MCU architecture.
